guide.summary: Chinese never moves words to make a question. Keep statement order and mark the question exactly once: add 吗, or double the verb (去不去), or offer a choice with 还是, or put a question word in the slot where the answer will go. One sentence, one question marker; that single idea removes most errors.

subs.label: 吗 vs A-not-A (去不去, 有没有)
subs.focus: Choose 吗 or A-not-A, or build the A-not-A form. Errors: both together (你去不去吗), 有不有 for 有没有, doubling the main verb instead of the modal (你想去不去), A-not-A after 也 / 都 / 很 where only 吗 works (你也去不去). Include 喜不喜欢, 可不可以 and 是不是 before a predicate.

subs.label: 还是 choice questions
subs.focus: The learner must pick 还是 for an either/or question and 或者 for 'or' in a statement, and must leave 吗 off a 还是 question. Classic mistakes: 你喝茶或者咖啡? and 你喝茶还是咖啡吗? Items may also test placing 还是 between the two parallel parts.

subs.label: Question words stay in place
subs.focus: Pick the right question word (谁, 什么, 哪 + measure, 哪儿, 什么时候) and put it in the answer's slot, not at the front, with no 吗. Errors: 什么你想吃?, 你去哪儿吗?, 什么时候 after the verb, 哪 without a measure word (哪书), 什么 where 哪 + measure is needed to choose among known items.

subs.label: 几 vs 多少
subs.focus: The learner must choose 几 or 多少. 几 expects a small number and must be followed by a measure word; 多少 is for any amount and can go straight before the noun. Classic mistakes: 几钱, 几学生 (no measure word), and 几 for clearly large numbers. Include the fixed uses: 几点, 几号, 星期几, 几岁, 多少钱.

subs.label: 怎么 vs 怎么样 vs 为什么
subs.focus: Choose 怎么 (how to, before a verb), 怎么样 (what it is like / how about it, as predicate) or 为什么 (why). Errors: 这个菜怎么?, 怎么样去 for method, 'how is…' with 怎么. Include 怎么 as surprised 'how come' before 不 / 没 / 还; the English cue must rule out 为什么 there.

subs.label: 多 + adjective (多大, 多长, 多远)
subs.focus: The learner must build 'how + adjective' with 多 and the right adjective: 多大 for age or size, 多长时间 or 多久 for duration, 多远 for distance, 多高, 多重. Classic mistakes: 怎么 + adjective (怎么远), 多少 + adjective (多少长), 多老 for age, and 很 left in the question. Items may also test the optional 有 before 多.

subs.label: Tag questions and 呢
subs.focus: Tags: 好吗 / 好不好 / 行吗 seek agreement to a suggestion; 对吗 / 对不对 / 是不是 / 是吗 check a fact; match tag to purpose. 呢: fits question-word, A-not-A and 还是 questions and a bare noun (你呢?), never with 吗 or on a plain statement. Errors: 你去哪儿吗?, 你是学生呢?, 好吗 to check a fact.

subs.label: Question words as 'any / every / nothing'
subs.focus: Use question word + 都 / 也 for 'everything, anyone, anywhere, nothing, nobody', with the question word before 都 / 也 even when it is the object. Errors: object left after the verb (我不想吃什么都), 都 / 也 dropped, reading it as a question. Include 没(有)什么 + noun and 也 / 都 + 不 / 没.

subs.label: Rhetorical 不是…吗
subs.focus: Recognise and build 不是 … 吗 as 'isn't it the case that…?', said when facts seem to contradict what the speaker believed. 不是 follows the subject, 吗 ends the sentence, and the middle keeps its own 不 or 了. Errors: dropping 吗, 不是 at the end, reading it as a real negative.

rules.rule: For a yes/no question, say the statement and add 吗. Nothing else changes.

examples.py: nǐ shì xué sheng ma
examples.en: Are you a student?

examples.py: nǐ míng tiān yǒu kòng ma
examples.en: Are you free tomorrow?

examples.py: nǐ men yě qù ma
examples.en: Are you going too?

rules.note: After 也, 都 or a degree word like 很, only 吗 is possible; A-not-A cannot follow them.

rules.rule: Or double the verb or adjective with 不 in between, and leave 吗 off. 有 doubles as 有没有. A two-syllable word usually doubles only its first syllable.

examples.py: nǐ míng tiān qù bù qù
examples.en: Are you going tomorrow or not?

examples.py: nǐ yǒu méi yǒu shí jiān
examples.en: Do you have time?

examples.py: nǐ xǐ bù xǐ huan hē chá
examples.en: Do you like drinking tea?

examples.py: zhè ge cài là bù là
examples.en: Is this dish spicy?

rules.note: The full form 喜欢不喜欢 is also correct, just less common. For a finished action ask with 没有: 你吃饭了没有? or 你吃没吃饭?

rules.rule: When there is a modal verb or 是, that is the word you double, not the verb after it.

examples.py: nǐ xiǎng bù xiǎng qù běi jīng
examples.en: Do you want to go to Beijing?

examples.py: nǐ huì bù huì kāi chē
examples.en: Can you drive?

examples.py: tā shì bù shì nǐ gē ge
examples.en: Is he your older brother?

examples.py: nǐ shì bù shì bù shū fu
examples.en: Are you feeling unwell?

rules.note: 是不是 can be put before any predicate to check a guess, which is the easy way to ask A-not-A about a sentence that already contains 不, 也 or 很.

rules.rule: Put 还是 between the two options to ask 'A or B?'. No 吗. 或者 is the 'or' of statements, not of questions.
rules.pattern: Subject + Option A + 还是 + Option B

examples.py: nǐ hē chá hái shi hē kā fēi
examples.en: Will you have tea or coffee?

examples.zh: 我们今天去还是明天去？
examples.py: wǒ men jīn tiān qù hái shi míng tiān qù
examples.en: Shall we go today or tomorrow?

examples.zh: 周末我常常看电影或者去爬山。
examples.py: zhōu mò wǒ cháng cháng kàn diàn yǐng huò zhě qù pá shān
examples.en: At weekends I often watch a film or go hiking.

rules.note: The second verb can be dropped when it is the same (你喝茶还是咖啡?). 还是 is also used when the choice is inside a statement of not knowing: 我不知道他今天来还是明天来。

rules.rule: Write the answer sentence, then replace the unknown part with the question word. The word order does not change and there is no 吗.

examples.py: nǐ zài zhǎo shén me
examples.en: What are you looking for?

examples.py: nǐ shén me shí hou huí guó
examples.en: When are you going back to your country?

examples.py: shéi jiāo nǐ men hàn yǔ
examples.en: Who teaches you Chinese?

examples.py: nǐ xiǎng mǎi nǎ běn shū
examples.en: Which book do you want to buy?

rules.note: 什么时候 sits where a time word sits: before the verb. 哪 needs a measure word (哪个, 哪本, 哪天). 哪儿 and 哪里 mean the same. 吗 after a question word is possible only when the word means 'something / anywhere' (你想吃点儿什么吗? 'Would you like something to eat?'), which is a different sentence.

rules.rule: 几 asks for a small number (roughly under ten) and always takes a measure word. 多少 asks for any amount and can stand directly before the noun.
rules.pattern: 几 + measure + Noun / 多少 + Noun

examples.py: nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén
examples.en: How many people are there in your family?

examples.py: nǐ men xué xiào yǒu duō shao xué sheng
examples.en: How many students does your school have?

examples.py: xiàn zài jǐ diǎn
examples.en: What time is it now?

examples.py: zhè jiàn yī fu duō shao qián
examples.en: How much is this piece of clothing?

rules.note: Fixed uses: 几点, 几号, 几月, 星期几, 几岁 (for a child), 多少钱, and 多少 for phone and room numbers. When the number could be small or large, 多少 is the safe choice; with a small expected number both are often heard (几个人 / 多少人).

rules.rule: 怎么 + verb asks the way to do something. 怎么样 is the predicate: what something is like, or 'how about it?'. 为什么 asks the reason.
rules.pattern: 怎么 + Verb / Topic + 怎么样 / 为什么 + Predicate

examples.py: zhè ge zì zěn me xiě
examples.en: How do you write this character?

examples.py: nà jiā fàn guǎn zěn me yàng
examples.en: What is that restaurant like?

examples.py: nǐ wèi shén me bù gào su wǒ
examples.en: Why didn't you tell me?

examples.py: nǐ zěn me hái méi shuì
examples.en: How come you're still not asleep?

rules.note: 怎么 before 不, 没, 还, 这么 or 了 means 'how come' and carries surprise; 为什么 is the neutral 'why' and fits in the same place. 你怎么了? means 'What's wrong with you?'.

rules.rule: For 'how old, how long, how far, how tall', put 多 before the adjective. An optional 有 may come before 多. No 很, no 怎么.

examples.py: nǐ ér zi duō dà le
examples.en: How old is your son?

examples.py: cóng zhè r dào jī chǎng yǒu duō yuǎn
examples.en: How far is it from here to the airport?

examples.py: nǐ xué le duō cháng shí jiān hàn yǔ
examples.en: How long have you studied Chinese?

examples.py: nǐ dì di duō gāo
examples.en: How tall is your younger brother?

rules.note: Use the 'big' adjective of the pair: 多大, 多长, 多远, 多高, 多重, never 多小 or 多短 for a neutral question. 多久 means the same as 多长时间. To an older person say 您多大年纪? rather than 你多大?

rules.rule: To turn a statement into a tag question, finish the sentence and add a short question. 好吗 / 好不好 / 行吗 ask someone to agree to a suggestion; 对吗 / 对不对 / 是不是 / 是吗 check a fact.
rules.pattern: Statement + 好吗 / 对不对 / 是不是

examples.py: wǒ men yī qǐ qù hǎo ma
examples.en: Let's go together, shall we?

examples.py: nǐ shì shàng hǎi rén duì bù duì
examples.en: You're from Shanghai, right?

examples.py: nǐ míng tiān bù shàng bān shì bù shì
examples.en: You're not working tomorrow, are you?

rules.note: The tag does not change with the sentence: a negative statement still takes 对不对 or 是不是, unlike English 'are you / aren't you'.

rules.rule: 呢 softens a question that already has a question word, an A-not-A form or 还是, and after a bare noun it asks 'and what about…?'. It never joins 吗 and cannot turn a plain statement into a yes/no question.
rules.pattern: Question-word question + 呢 / Noun + 呢

examples.py: nǐ zài kàn shén me ne
examples.en: What are you looking at?

examples.py: wǒ hěn hǎo nǐ ne
examples.en: I'm fine, and you?

examples.py: tā zěn me hái méi lái ne
examples.en: Why hasn't he come yet?

examples.py: wǒ de shǒu jī ne
examples.en: Where's my phone?

rules.note: 呢 on these questions is optional; it adds a thoughtful or puzzled tone. With no earlier context, Noun + 呢 asks where the thing is.

rules.rule: Question word + 都 / 也 means 'every / any'; with 不 or 没 after it, 'no / none'. The question word must stand before 都 / 也, so an object moves in front of the verb.
rules.pattern: Subject + Question word + 都 / 也 + (不 / 没) + Verb

examples.py: zhè jiàn shì shéi dōu zhī dào
examples.en: Everyone knows about this.

examples.py: wǒ jīn tiān shén me dōu bù xiǎng chī
examples.en: I don't feel like eating anything today.

examples.py: zhōu mò wǒ nǎ r yě méi qù
examples.en: I didn't go anywhere at the weekend.

examples.py: wǒ méi shén me wèn tí
examples.en: I don't really have any questions.

rules.note: In positive sentences use 都 (谁都知道); 也 is mostly for negatives, where 都 is equally fine. 没(有)什么 + noun stays after the verb and means 'not much, nothing in particular'.

rules.rule: 不是 … 吗 does not ask and does not negate: it reminds the listener of something the speaker believes is true, often with surprise. Put 不是 after the subject and 吗 at the end.

examples.py: nǐ bù shì shuō jīn tiān lái ma
examples.en: Didn't you say you were coming today?

examples.py: tā bù shì yǐ jīng huí guó le ma
examples.en: Hasn't he already gone back to his country?

examples.zh: 你不是不喜欢吃辣的吗？
examples.py: nǐ bù shì bù xǐ huan chī là de ma
examples.en: I thought you didn't like spicy food?

rules.note: The part between 不是 and 吗 is what the speaker thinks is true, so it keeps its own 不, 没 or 了.

right.py: nǐ míng tiān qù bù qù

contrasts.why: 去不去 is already the question. 吗 and A-not-A never appear together.

right.py: nǐ yǒu méi yǒu shí jiān

contrasts.why: 有 is negated only with 没, so its A-not-A form is 有没有.
A-not-A cannot follow 也, 都 or 很. With those adverbs ask with 吗.

right.en: What do you want to eat?

contrasts.why: The question word stays where the answer goes: after 吃, as its object. It does not move to the front as in English.
哪儿 already makes it a question. To soften it use 呢, not 吗.

right.py: nǐ xiǎng hē chá hái shi kā fēi
right.en: Would you like tea or coffee?

contrasts.why: 'Or' that asks the listener to choose is 还是. 或者 only lists alternatives in a statement.

right.en: How much money do you have?

contrasts.why: 几 must be followed by a measure word and expects a small number. An open amount with no measure word takes 多少.

right.py: zhè ge cài zěn me yàng

contrasts.why: 'How is it?' asks what something is like, which is 怎么样. 怎么 needs a verb after it and asks the way of doing.

right.py: nǐ nǚ ér duō dà le

contrasts.why: Age is asked with 多大. 老 means elderly, so 多老 does not ask someone's age.

right.py: wǒ shén me dōu bù xiǎng chī
right.en: I don't want to eat anything.

contrasts.why: The question word must come before 都, so the object 什么 moves in front of the verb.

cheat: One question marker per sentence: 吗, or A-not-A, or 还是, or a question word. Never two.
Question word goes where the answer goes. Don't move it to the front.
也 / 都 / 很 in the sentence? Use 吗, not A-not-A. With a modal, double the modal: 想不想去.
Asking someone to choose: 还是. 'Or' in a statement: 或者.
几 + measure word for small numbers; 多少 for anything else and for 钱.
怎么 + verb = how to; 怎么样 = how is it; 多 + adjective = how big / long / far.
什么 / 谁 / 哪儿 before 都 or 也 is not a question: it means every / any / none.
